    A person is a resident alien of the United States for tax purposes if they meet either the green card test or the substantial presence test for the calendar year. This is known as the “green card” test per page 4 of Publication 519. A taxpayer is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time if they have been given the privilege, according to the immigration laws, of residing permanently in the United States as an immigrant. A taxpayer has this status if the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) (or its predecessor organization) has issued the taxpayer an alien registration card, also known as a “green card.”nnPer page 11 of Publication 519, a resident alien’s income is generally subject to tax in the same manner as a U.S. citizen. A nonresident alien usually is subject to U.S. income tax only on U.S. source income.nnIn this case, whether or not a taxpayer is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time during calendar year 2024 is the green card test. Mailing income tax returns to the Internal Revenue Service using the Certified Mail Return Receipt Requested at the U.S. Post Office is a good idea to prove timely filing and receipt of the income tax returns, but it is not the green card test.
